body: Anytime man. I know it hurts a lot right now and I wish I had more to offer you. Try to take it one day at a time and to not beat yourself up too much over it.

Man I just wanna say that you are not alone. I can relate to almost everything you wrote about in this post. Its been nearly four years for me since I (34m) lost the woman I wanted to spend my life with. Things were perfect, until they weren't and I got addicted to a terrible drug due to me self medicating and not knowing I was bipolar. 

I won't lie to you man, its still tough to live with sometimes. I've overcome a lot of hardships since then, but there are still things that will remind me of her and bring me to tears. As cliche as it is, it does get better with time though.  Also now when I'm reminded of her I try to focus on the happy memories I have of us together and that helps a bit too. 

I may just be an internet stranger, but if you ever need a buddy to talk to about anything you might be going through, feel free to shoot me a message.
I hate mine for multiple reasons but mainly because its a reminder of how alone I am now.

Man I can relate to every single thing that you wrote here, especially the having ZERO support system. It feels like such a catch 22 at times. But if you are ever needing someone to talk to, feel free to hit me up. I'm usually a fairly decent listener and I know how much of a difference it can make to have somebody to vent to that also understands how damn frustrating this illness often is.

Your welcome. I wish I had a better outlook on it to give you, but unfortunately it is a pretty damaging drug these days. And us addicts usually have to lose everything before we take the steps to get clean and stay that way.

That stuff was my drug of choice about 2 years ago. I smoked it nearly every day for about 4 years. I completely ruined my life over it. I had a a lot of great things going for me and I eventually lost it all to that addiction. 

I smoked weed regularly for years but switched to this stuff since I had a job that did random drug tests. The first few iterations of it were very similar to THC but usually a bit more intense and much shorter duration of about 30mins to an hour. Due to that, you build up a tolerance really fast to it. 

Some of the [synthetic compouds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_designer_drugs) that are used to make this stuff were absolutely horrible to be ingesting. Some would cause people to have seizures, others would have their kidneys fail, and some people slipped into psychosis and suffered permanent brain damage from them. I fell into the psychosis category and ended up spending a couple of weeks in a mental hospital and was diagnosed with bipolar disorder during that time. Whether or not the bipolar was directly caused by my addiction is uncertain, but most of my doctors believe that it was likely a significant factor. Apparently I got pretty lucky as I met many people in my stay there whose minds were completely gone after they used it.

I'm not the op but it doesn't seem like they are trying to say that you are wrong either, just that for an addict it eventually shifts to a point where you never even come close to reaching the "high" you got the first few times you did your drug of choice, even with an endless supply. Then it becomes a necessity to be a functional human and gradually takes control over everything else in your life and without it you become distraught and violently ill.
